references.text: The cloud that lifted from the tabernacle was a sign to the Israelites to break camp, and when it did not lift, they remained. This establishes the fundamental principle that the people followed the movements of the cloud.

The preceding verse describes how the Israelites broke camp when the cloud lifted and pitched their tents where the cloud stopped - this complements verse 18, which repeats the principle of following the Lord's command.

Elaborates on the theme that the Israelites followed the movements of the cloud - whether it stayed for two days, a month, or longer - they pitched camp and broke camp according to the word of the Lord.
Describes how the people broke camp for the first time at the Lord's command through Moses, as a practical application of the principle in 9:18.
Moses reminds the people how the Lord went before them on the way to show them where they should pitch camp, in fire by night and in a cloud by day.
The cloud that filled the Lord's house at the dedication of the temple is a parallel to the cloud over the tabernacle that led Israel.
The psalm describes how God led the people with a cloud by day and with the light of fire by night, as a poetic rendering of the same historical phenomenon.
Refers to how God spread out a cloud as a covering and fire to give light at night - a praise of God's guidance of Israel.
Isaiah prophesies about a cloud by day and smoke and the shining of flaming fire by night over Mount Zion, as an eschatological echo of the wilderness journey.
Paul refers to how all the fathers were under the cloud and passed through the sea, using this as a typological example for Christians.
